text:
andrew: Heads-up — long-context soak on Dedicated shows steady KV memory growth after ~30k tokens. Repro with batch=16, batch_window_ms=20, max_seq=32768.
perf-bot: perf job rdw-longcontext-901 finished — artifacts: https://ci.redwood/rdw-longcontext-901 :artifacts: 
mar ia: Can you paste the small profiler summary and allocator info?
andrew: sure — ran with jemalloc, hugepages disabled. Key metric is the KV reuse histogram changed over time. Short snippet below.
```
# initial (0-5k tokens) KV reuse histogram
0-4: 62%
5-16: 24%
17-64: 10%
65+: 4%
# after 30k tokens
0-4: 45%
5-16: 18%
17-64: 17%
65+: 20%
```
sam: wow 65+ bin jumped to 20% — that's big. Hosted runs don't show that?
andrew: correct. Hosted (gce) run with same model and batch settings stayed stable. Dedicated (aws/g4-like) drifted.
olga: any perf counters? pagewalks, major/minor faults?
andrew: pagemap pagewalks/sec +3x at the onset of the growth. Major faults stayed low. Eviction sweeper activity also shows bursty runs: sweeper triggered infrequently then reclaimed large swaths.
maria: could be config drift on eviction thresholds or background compaction cadence. We saw similar behaviour when sweeper was too lazy.
andrew: found it — dedicated config had eviction.threshold: 12 (percent free) vs hosted 6. That explains the big reclaim waves when free memory finally hit 12%.
kevin: confirmed: /etc/redwood/kv.yaml on Dedicated AMI differs from our hosted image. Looks like a packaging oversight from the reserved pool image.
perf-bot: perf counter dump (selected):
```
pmu.pagewalks: 1200 -> 3600 (spike)
page_alloc_trylocks: +signal
kv_sweeper_runs: 2/min (before), 0.1/min (during growth)
```
maria: Also worth noting batching/window interaction: larger batch.window_ms increases slot residency which raises effective working set. If eviction threshold is high, free slabs dwindle and fragmentation increases rather than steady reclaim.
sam: What about Private/on-prem GPUs? Any difference?
andrew: on-prem (driver 535, kernel 6.1) interestingly had lower net KV growth but more fragmentation — contiguous page allocations are smaller because of NUMA/cgroup settings. We saw higher softirq/CPU stall events around large evictions (PCIe bandwidth thrash), but not the steady climb we saw on Dedicated.
olga: Possible causes across envs: (a) eviction.threshold drift, (b) MTU/driver/kernel page alignment differences, (c) allocator (jemalloc) behavior under pinned GPU memory, (d) batching/window sizing.
kevin: action: align eviction.threshold to 6 in Dedicated canary and monitor. Also will check AMI packaging pipeline.
andrew: repro steps + commands I'm using: 
```
# client long context
rdw-client --env=dedicated --model=redwood-v2 --batch=16 --batch-window-ms=20 --max-tokens=32768 --long-context
# collect kv hist
rdw-prof --collect-kv-histogram --out=/tmp/kv_hist.json
# tail sweeper log
tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/kv-sweeper.log
```
maria: propose matrix test: envs=[hosted,dedicated,private], batch=[1,8,16], window_ms=[5,20,50], eviction.threshold=[4,6,12], run until 100k tokens or 6 hours. Sam can run hosted matrix, Andrew runs dedicated, Olga does private.
andrew: will do dedicated runs after canary change. I also uploaded full perf artifacts to the job link above.
kevin: deploy-bot applied canary config change to Dedicated: /etc/redwood/kv.yaml eviction.threshold=6 — canary group id rdw-canary-17.
deploy-bot: config-change applied to Dedicated canary: /etc/redwood/kv.yaml eviction.threshold=6 :white_check_mark:
andrew: re-running a 48h soak on canary now, batch=16 window=20. Will report histograms + pagemap traces.
olga: long-term mitigations: 1) auto-adaptive sweeper that uses reuse histogram to pick sweep intensity; 2) MTU-aware page allocator fallback for VPC/on-prem edge cases; 3) package parity checks in AMI build pipeline; 4) add eviction.threshold to our config drift monitor (console alert).
maria: please open RFC/issue with perf artifacts + repro scripts. Assign owners as discussed.
andrew: done — opened RFC 2026-kv-reuse-adaptive with links to perf artifacts and the run matrix plan. Assigning to andrew/sam/olga/kevin.
sam: I'll start hosted matrix tomorrow and attach logs.
andrew: thanks — I'll post interim histograms here.
